answer: Each identity links to one distinct certified lifeguard, marked at the vertex of its patrol sector, who flies a sable flag and logs shifts beside a relic rescue board whose serial the agency photographs monthly. The certifying body cross-checks the licence serial, tower captain sign-off and a random live rescue drill; a missed drill or shared licence revokes the slot. One guard cannot staff two towers at once, so 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 certified guards, $450 in course and exam fees each ($450,000) plus 12,000 patrol hours monthly. Trade-off: inland and winter agents qualify slowly.
